commandList:
List of commands used in the PARAM.in file for MITTENS configured as the PT component of the SWMF. MITTENS (Monte carlo Integration of Turbulent Transport and ENergization of SEPs) solves the stochastic differential equations equivalent to the isotropic Parker transport equation on a 1D Lagrangian grid along interplanetary magnetic field lines. This file was rewritten 2026-08-05 to match the actual command readers in src/; the previous version was inherited from MFLAMPA (SP) and documented many commands MITTENS does not read.
#STARTTIME 2013 iYear 4 iMonth 11 iDay 0 iHour 0 iMinute 0 iSecond
Sets the initial date and time of the simulation. Together with the simulation time this determines the real date and time of the modeled state, used e.g. to timestamp output. The default is 2000-3-21 10:45:00, the same as in the SWMF.
#NSTEP 0 nStep
Sets the iteration counter. Useful for restarts. Default is 0.
#TIMESIMULATION 0.0 PTTime [s]
Sets the simulation time in seconds. Useful for restarts. The data input time is initialized to the same value. Default is 0.
#TIMEACCURATE T DoTimeAccurate
Accepted for compatibility with standard SWMF parameter files. MITTENS only supports time-accurate mode: the value must be true (the code stops with an explanatory message if false).
#RUN
Executes the commands read so far as one session and continues reading the parameter file afterwards. Without #RUN the whole file forms one session.
#END
Signals the end of the parameter file: reading stops here.
#STOP 5000 nIterMax 3600.0 TimeMax [s]
Sets the stopping conditions of the run: maximum number of iterations (MHD state advances) and maximum simulation time in seconds. A negative value disables the corresponding condition. In stand alone mode this command is required.
#CHECKSTOPFILE T UseStopFile
If true (default), the code checks for the existence of a MITTENS.STOP file in the run directory at the end of each iteration and stops gracefully when it is found.
#CPUTIMEMAX 86000.0 CpuTimeMax [s]
Maximum wall clock time of the run in seconds. When exceeded, the run stops gracefully. Useful for batch queues. Negative (default) disables the check.
#DORUN T DoRun
If DoRun is false, the background state is read and processed but the particle distribution function is not solved. The default is true.
#TEST F DoRunTest
If true, run the analytic field line test: an analytic shock is set up (see PT_ModShock::get_test_shock) and the sampled distribution function is saved for comparison against the analytic steady state solution instead of the regular plot output. Default is false.
#RESTART T DoRestart
Signals that the run is restarted. NOTE: writing and reading of restart files is not yet implemented in MITTENS; this command only sets the flag.
#COORDSYSTEM HGR TypeCoordSystem
Sets the coordinate system of the field line data (converted to upper case on reading), e.g. HGR, HGI, GSM. Any string is accepted; the code does not currently transform between systems.
#FIELDLINEGRID 4 nLat 4 nLon
Sets the angular grid of field lines: nLat x nLon lines in total. The lines are distributed over the MPI processors in contiguous blocks.
#ORIGIN 2.5 ROrigin [Rs] 0.0 LonMin [deg] -70.0 LatMin [deg] 360.0 LonMax [deg] 70.0 LatMax [deg]
Origin points of the traced field lines on the surface R=ROrigin, in the given longitude and latitude intervals. Only used in coupled (SWMF) mode; ignored in stand alone mode, where the field line geometry comes from the input data files.
#READMHDATA T DoReadMhData MH_data NameInputDir 1 iLonFile 1 iLatFile
Read the field line background (MFLAMPA-format MH_data files) from NameInputDir. iLonFile and iLatFile select the longitude and latitude indices in the input file names, MH_data_iLon_iLat_tag.out (or .dat). The remaining parameters are read only if DoReadMhData is true.
#MHDATA ascii TypeFile MH_data.lst NameTagFile
Sets the format of the MHD input files and the name of the file (inside NameInputDir) containing the list of time tags, one file per time level. Reading is tag file driven: each iteration consumes the next tag. If the tag file is temporarily exhausted the code waits for it to be appended (real time mode) and aborts if no new tag appears within 10 minutes. NameTagFile is only used when UseAppendedRead is false in #APPENDMHDATA.
#APPENDMHDATA T UseAppendedRead
If UseAppendedRead is true, the field line background is read from a single file with all time levels appended (MH_data_iLon_iLat.out, as written by MFLAMPA with UseAppendedWrite): each iteration reads the next appended block instead of consuming a tag from NameTagFile, and the run stops when the end of the file is reached. The default is false, i.e. tag file driven reading of one file per time level.
#SHOCK T DoSharpenShock 50 nSearchMax 0.01 dLogRhoThreshold
Controls shock tracking. The shock is located at the maximum of the density gradient (dLogRho) searched within nSearchMax cells of its previous position; the up/downstream extent of the shock zone is found by walking away from the maximum while dLogRho exceeds dLogRhoThreshold. If DoSharpenShock is true, the smeared compression across the detected zone is condensed onto two cells. WARNING: the analytic width scan (Doc/shock_grid_resolution_notes.md) shows a 1-2 cell discontinuity biases the DSA spectrum (slope -4.6 instead of -4.0 for r=4); a smooth profile at least 3 cells wide is required for unbiased acceleration, so sharpening onto 2 cells currently puts runs into the biased regime.
#PARTICLE 10 nInject T UseSplit 4 nSplit 0.1 SplitEnergyMin [MeV] 100.0 SplitEnergyMax [MeV]
Particle injection and splitting. nInject particles are injected at the shock each time the shock advances one Lagrangian cell. If UseSplit is true, particles are split (weight conserving) as they cross nSplit logarithmically spaced energy levels between SplitEnergyMin and SplitEnergyMax, increasing high energy statistics.
#INPUTSEED F UseInputSeedFile
If true, the pseudo random number generator state of each processor is set from the file seed.in in the run directory, making runs reproducible. Two formats are accepted: (1) a single integer, the master seed, from which every rank derives its own independent stream (Param/seed.in is an example; this is the form to use for frozen-seed runs and tests), or (2) one line per rank with 5 integers, "iProc State1 State2 State3 State4", exactly as written to PT/IO2/seed.out by a previous run (used to continue that run). A per-rank file must have exactly one record per rank; files in any other format, or giving all ranks the same state, stop the code. If false (default), seeds are drawn from /dev/urandom. In either case the states used are saved to PT/IO2/seed.out.
#SDE 1.0 TimeStepFactor 0.01 MaxTimeStep [s]
Controls the Euler-Maruyama particle time step. The locally computed adaptive time step candidate is multiplied by TimeStepFactor and capped at MaxTimeStep. There are no code defaults; this command is required. With #DISTANCETIMESTEP off, MaxTimeStep acts as the de facto uniform step and must resolve the shock kick (see Doc/timestep_notes.md for the measured cost of setting it too large). With #DISTANCETIMESTEP on, the distance ramp provides the near shock control and MaxTimeStep can be raised to the MHD coupling cadence.
#DISTANCETIMESTEP T UseDistanceTimestep 0.1 AlphaDist
Distance aware adaptive particle time step. When enabled, each particle's time step is additionally limited by (i) a distance ramp dt = AlphaDist*d\^2/(2*KappaLagr), where d is the Lagrangian distance to the shock center or to either end of the line (floored at one cell), so that a single step's diffusive displacement never exceeds sqrt(AlphaDist) times the distance to the nearest structure; (ii) a shock motion guard dt = d/(2*VShock); and (iii) a compression rate guard dt = AlphaDist/|dLogRho/dt|. AlphaDist (read only when enabled) is the single safety factor: 0.1 gives converged spectra (validated for compression ratios 2, 3 and 4 on smooth analytic shocks at 6-12x speedup); larger values trade accuracy for speed (0.3 reproduces the uniform dt=0.01 s accuracy at 17x). Default is off. NOTE: enabling changes the random number consumption sequence, so results can only be compared to reference solutions statistically, not bit for bit.
#DIFFUSION MHD UpstreamDxxModel 0.03 CorrelationLength [AU] 1.0 ScalingFactor F UseConstantDiffusion
Selects the spatial diffusion coefficient model. UpstreamDxxModel is one of: MHD (Dxx computed from the local MHD state and turbulence level), PSP (the analytic PSP-calibrated radial parameterization of Chen et al. 2024), or Analytical (constant mean free path Lambda0 in AU, read only for this model). CorrelationLength is the turbulence correlation length at 1 AU and ScalingFactor multiplies the resulting Dxx. If UseConstantDiffusion is true, DxxConst is read and overrides the model with a spatially constant diffusion coefficient. There is no default model; this command is required.
#BOUNDARY reflect BoundaryInner absorb BoundaryOuter
Particle boundary conditions at the inner (first Lagrangian vertex) and outer (last vertex) end of each field line: reflect or absorb. There are no code defaults; this command is required.
#ADVECTION T UseLogScaling
If true (default), the adiabatic momentum kick from compression is applied in logarithmic (exact exponential) form; if false, the linearized update is used.
#DISTRIBUTION 200 nEnergyBins 10.0 eBinMin [keV] 1.0e6 eBinMax [keV] 10.0 InjEnergy [keV] 1.0 InjCoeff
Phase space binning of the sampled distribution function: nEnergyBins logarithmic energy bins between eBinMin and eBinMax (in keV). Particles are injected at InjEnergy (keV); InjCoeff sets the injection amplitude used in the normalization of the distribution function. This command is required.
#SDEBINNING T DoBinEntireFieldline 400 nLagrBins 10.0 BinTimeWindow [s]
Spatial binning of the sampled distribution. If DoBinEntireFieldline is true, the whole field line is divided into nLagrBins Lagrangian bins; otherwise a single bin of width BinWidthLagr (Lagrangian cells) centered at radius BinCenterRs (Rs) is used. Samples are accumulated over BinTimeWindow seconds before each output (occupation time weighted, i.e. each particle contributes weight*dt per step).
#SAVEOUTPUT
Reserved for output control parameters; currently reads nothing.
